title: analysis.state.snapshot result
description: One machine's reviewed state, named. This document is also an input: `analysis.state.compare` reads it back, including one written by something other than this toolkit.

image_id.description: The image whose variables were decoded.

regions.description: The ranges of memory the snapshot read, each with the digest of the bytes it actually got.

source.description: The identity the range was read from, so a snapshot says which file it described rather than only which addresses.

registers.description: The register file the snapshot was taken with — the shape a call record reports its outputs in, because that is where a caller pastes it from. A base-register global's address is a register plus a displacement, so a project holding any is refused without this rather than read at whatever zero points at.

fields.description: Every leaf value, in path order. An aggregate contributes its leaves and no row of its own: a struct has no value, only fields that do.

path.description: `name`, `name.field`, `name[3].field` — stable, and what a comparison aligns on. Never an address: two runs under different load maps hold the same state at different addresses.

address.description: Where this leaf was read from in the snapshot's address space.

type_id.description: The type the project gives it, so a consumer can tell a byte from a signed byte without re-deriving it.

object_sha256.description: The object digest the annotation naming this was established against.

value.description: What one leaf holds. Tagged, and deliberately not collapsed into a number: a pointer that compared equal to an integer of the same bit pattern would let a relocated address read as an unchanged value.

member.description: The name the project gives this value, when it names one. Absent means the stored number is not one the project enumerates, which is a finding rather than an error.

hex.description: Bytes, for a leaf whose type states a width this build cannot read as a scalar. Reported rather than skipped, so the field still appears in a comparison and still says it changed.

fields_total.description: Leaves the snapshot decoded before the report cap.

fields_truncated.description: Whether the reported fields are a prefix. A comparison against a capped snapshot cannot tell an absent field from a truncated one, and says so.
